target: Route "width-amortise": bounded treewidth, the amortisation statement (labels wa:) — results wa:recursion, wa:pi + wa:amortised, wa:warm-measured, wa:fold3, wa:forest-response + wa:forest-poly, wa:forest-k1, wa:qp-measured, wa:tw2-open

findings.defect: PI_k is EQUIVALENT to the conclusion of wa:amortised, not a weaker hypothesis: the converse implication is trivial and is nowhere noticed, so the route's "corrected gap" is target-equivalent to the bounded-treewidth restriction of prob:main and must be declared as such (rule 4, and the paper's own convention that a route ending at a target-equivalent statement has ended at the target). rem wa:pi-is-the-pivot's assertion that "PI_k alone gives nothing without the recursion of wa:amortised" mis-states the relation, and the headline "the width route lands on the pivot" is wrong: it lands on the (restricted) target.
findings.evidence: Trivial converse. Assume wa:amortised's conclusion: stopping payoff games of treewidth <= k, given with a decomposition, are solved exactly in time poly(n, log Delta). Given H, X with |X| <= k+1, dyadic theta, theta' and ANY optimal pair of H[X:=theta], discard the input pair and solve H[X:=theta'] directly: it is a stopping payoff game (lem:cut-sign), Gamma(H[X:=theta']) = Gamma(H) - X is an induced subgraph so its treewidth is <= k, and a width-k decomposition is obtained by deleting X from every bag of the given one; output the greedy pair, which is optimal because T_sigma val = val and T_sigma has a unique fixed point on a stopping game (thm:contraction with lem:payoff-transfer(a),(b)). This is exactly PI_k. Hence PI_k <=> "stopping payoff games of treewidth <= k are in P". Corroboration from the route's own results: PI_1 is TRUE, immediately, by wa:forest-poly (Gamma(H[X:=theta']) is a forest, so val is computed with O(m) exact operations and the greedy pair is optimal) — yet next_steps item 4 proposes "is PI_1 true" as the natural first target for a future round. Scripts: /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/d1fe2115-9b72-4784-bb94-87421ac1106c/scratchpad/audit-width-amortise-correctness/forest.py, t_forest.py (PI_1's solver replicated and cross-checked against brute-force max-min on 320 forest games, 0 mismatches).

findings.defect: The gap statement, offered as the route's one-sentence deliverable, is false as literally written: the time bound q(m+B) omits the bit-size beta of H's own terminal payoffs, so in the bit model no algorithm can meet it, and wa:amortised is then vacuously true. Repairable by q(m+B+beta) (or by counting arithmetic operations, the paper's convention in thm:qp); the equivalence of the previous finding is with the repaired version.
findings.evidence: Counterexample to PI_1 as written. H has non-terminals x (average, x -> (t0,t1)) and v (Max, v -> (x, T_p) with T_p a terminal of payoff p of bit-size beta); Gamma(H) is the single edge {v,x}, a forest, and H is stopping. Take X = {x}, theta = 0, theta' = 1/2, so m = 2 and B = 2. An optimal action of v in H[x:=1/2] is x iff 1/2 >= p, so the output determines the comparison of p with 1/2, which needs Omega(beta) bit operations; q(m+B) = q(4) is a constant.

findings.defect: The last query of a node is not covered by PI_k and is not in the cost accounting: after lem:round-recover the node holds theta* = val_G|_X, a rational of denominator up to 2*Delta*2^a and in general NOT dyadic, whereas def wa:pi quantifies over dyadic theta, theta' only; thm:qp obtains the values off X by "one more round of recursive solves", which the route's per-node cost ("one recursive call per component plus O(B^{k+1})(q + poly)") does not include. Repairable (two cold solves per component, i.e. Q = 2, and wa:recursion(a) still gives a polynomial), but as written the step is asserted.
findings.evidence: Route proof text: "Every later query theta of the search is answered by applying PI_k to each C_i ...  The rounding, the thm:tarski search, the continued-fraction recovery of lem:round-recover and the final check T_G w = w are unchanged". frontier.tex l.3073ff (thm:qp) needs "exact recovery and one more round of recursive solves"; the recovered vector is the one lem:round-recover produces as "the unique rational of denominator at most Q", not a grid point.

findings.defect: FL(D) is not fully defined and the printed path decomposition does not cover its interaction graph. The definition sets F_0 := u but never gives u's kind or out-edges, although (i) |V| = D^2+4D+3 counts u, (ii) "FL(D) is stopping" is a statement about the unfrozen game and the stopping proof handles every vertex except u, and (iii) Gamma(FL(D)) contains the edge {X_1,u} as soon as u is a non-terminal — an edge the stated bag list, whose first two bags "are replaced by {X_1},{X_1,Y_1} at d=1", never covers.
findings.evidence: With the P_D reading (u in Vavg, u -> (t0,t1)) everything else checks out, but my bag-by-bag checker reports "edges not covered: [['X1','u']]" for every D = 1..9; with u added to the first bag the decomposition is valid with all bags of size <= 4 (width 3) for D = 1..9. findings.defect: The warm column of the table does not reproduce. The cold column reproduces exactly under the natural protocol; the warm column comes out uniformly one smaller than any natural count I can construct, and the statement gives no protocol from which the discrepancy can be settled.
findings.evidence: Protocol recovered from the statement: bisection of [0,1] with 2D+2 midpoint queries, Hoffman-Karp = exact Min best response (backward induction, the frozen games are acyclic) + all-switches, cold start sigma = first successor. Cold totals for D = 2..12 come out 5,9,13,18,24,31,39,48,58,69,81 on BOTH P_D and FL(D) — the route's numbers exactly (bisection target 2/3; target 1/3 gives 6 at D=2 and the same thereafter). Warm totals come out 1,2,4,7,11,16,22,29,37,46,56 excluding the first query and 2,4,7,11,16,... including it; the route's 1,3,6,10,15,21,28,36,45,55,66 = D(D-1)/2 is exactly one MORE than my excluding-column would need and exactly one LESS than my including-column, at every D. Script hk.py.

findings.evidence: Max rounds over the 2^D piece midpoints = D for D = 2..8 on both families from sigma = first successor and from sigma = second successor; exhaustively over all 2^D starting strategies for D = 2..5 the worst case is D and the BEST start still needs D. Along the bisection sequence the max is D-1 for D = 2..12, as claimed. Script hk.py.

findings.defect: The measurement does not vary the parameter PI_k turns on. P_D and FL(D) have |Vmax| = D, and the observed Hoffman-Karp cost is exactly D; so the cost is pinned by the number of Max vertices, not by the piece count, and the experiment says nothing about the difficulty of SELECTING the switches, which is what PI_k asks for. The route's caveat names random sampling but not this.
findings.evidence: |Vmax| = D in both families (F_1..F_D); measured cold and warm HK rounds are at most D at every theta (verified D <= 8), i.e. the run length equals the number of Max vertices. The random-game half of the proposition compares warm against cold Hoffman-Karp, which is a comparison of two heuristics, not a probe of the worst case.

findings.defect: The table contradicts the sentence it is offered to support, and is not reproducible (random instances, no seed).
findings.evidence: Route's own numbers: treewidth 2, n=20 at depth 2 gives 84.0 queries / 400.8 solves while n=16 at depth 1 gives 124.2 / 1107.8, and n=28 at depth 2 gives 1060.5 / 4208.0 against n=24's 147639 / 310323. So the counts do not "jump by three to four orders of magnitude when the recursion depth goes from 1 to 2"; the spread is instance variance. wa:recursion is a pure analysis in any case, so the empirical support is decorative.

findings.defect: The refutation of the paper's amortisation sentence is reading-dependent, and part (b) bounds the recursion, not any algorithm.
findings.evidence: Under "total <= poly(n) x (cost of one query)" the route is right and wa:recursion(b) applies; under "total <= (cost of one query) + poly(n)" the sentence does yield polynomiality — and that reading is precisely the scheme of wa:amortised, so the route half-refutes and half-proves the paper's sentence without saying so. wa:recursion(b) assumes "the recursion is tight" and (silently) T(n_0) >= 1; it therefore gives a lower bound on the solution of the recurrence, not on the running time of thm:qp's procedure, so "it cannot be improved" is a statement about the bound only.

findings.defect: Two citations are to results stated for stopping SSGs but applied to stopping PAYOFF games, without invoking the transfer lemma; and the negative conclusion "treewidth one is not a new polynomial class" holds only for stopping games.
findings.evidence: thm:bounded-components (frontier.tex l.4129) defines K_k as "the class of SSGs ..." and thm:short-path (l.3391) begins "Let G be a stopping SSG"; lem:payoff-transfer(b) supplies the transfer but is not cited for either. Separately, wa:forest-poly needs no stopping hypothesis while wa:forest-k1's trap argument does: the non-stopping forest game u -> (w,t0), w -> (u,t0) with u,w in Vmax has mutually reachable Max vertices and is not in K_1, so on non-stopping forest games wa:forest-poly is not subsumed by thm:bounded-components.

Building FW(D) from the printed edges (H_d -> (t0,H'_d), H'_d -> (t0,H_{d-1}), H_0 -> (t0,t1), Y_d -> (H_{d-1},G_{d-1}), X_d -> (t0,F_{d-1})) needs H_0..H_{D-1} and H'_1..H'_{D-1}, giving |V| = 6D+2, not 6D+3. Everything else in the remark reproduces: FW(D) is stopping, its response has exactly 2^D pieces with slopes {0,2^{-D}}, exact treewidth 3 at D=2,3 and min-fill width 4 for D=4..12.

verdict:
One MAJOR defect survives, so the route is not sound as reported; everything computational, however, reproduced.

WHAT REPRODUCED (rebuilt from the statements, exact Fractions, in /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/d1fe2115-9b72-4784-bb94-87421ac1106c/scratchpad/audit-width-amortise-correctness/):
- wa:fold3 in full. FL(D) built from wa:def-fl: |V| = D^2+4D+3 (D=1..7), stopping (greatest trap empty, lem:trapchar) for D=1..7; the response at F_D computed by an independent symbolic piecewise-affine backward induction equals 2^{-(D+1)}(theta + 1 - 2^{-D} + 2^{-D} T^D(theta)) coefficient-for-coefficient for D=1..7, with exactly 2^D pieces, breakpoints exactly j/2^D and slope set {0, 2^{-D}}; cross-checked against DAG backward induction at the eight rationals 1/3, 2/7, 5/11, 1/2, 3/4, 17/64, 9/32, 100/257 for D<=6 and against brute-force componentwise max-min over all positional pairs for D<=3: 0 mismatches. The same engine reproduces thm:fold's closed form on P_D for D<=7. Width: the K_4 minor A={X1,F1,X2}, B={G1,Y2}, C={F2,X3,F3,Y3}, E={G2} verified disjoint, connected and pairwise adjacent for D=3..9, so tw>=3; the path decomposition is valid at width 3 once u is put in a bag (see the minor finding). Independent confirmation that FL genuinely lowers the width: min-fill gives elimination width 3 for FL(D), D=3..9, and width 4 for P_D, D=4..12 (exact subset-DP treewidth: tw(P_2)=tw(P_3)=3, tw(FL_1)=tw(FL_2)=2). So FL(D) does answer rem:fold-width's open question, 2^{Omega(sqrt N)} pieces at treewidth = pathwidth 3.
- wa:forest-response / wa:forest-poly. Proof reconstructed line by line (all five cases of the least fixed point, the induction on the tree, the nonempty-ness of {x : h(x) <= x} from h(1)<=1); implemented from the statement and cross-checked against brute-force max-min: 200 random forest games (170 of them NON-stopping) with 5032 exact response checks, 120 larger games (n=12..30, four distinct terminal payoffs) and 120 games with 13650 dense response checks on a 42-point grid — 0 mismatches anywhere, maximum branch-response piece count 2 in every case (the 28 apparent three-run responses were all a single grid cell straddling the one breakpoint). The halving chain at n=60 returns 2^{-60}. No coefficient or breakpoint denominator ever exceeded 2*Delta*2^a in 400 further games at n=40..80.
- wa:forest-k1. The trap argument is correct as printed (every internal z_i has both z_{i-1},z_{i+1} as successors, so its out-degree is exhausted; the endpoints are controlled with a successor in U; U is a nonempty trap). The sharpness witness reproduces exactly: stopping, values (2/3,2/3,1/3,1/3), Gamma a 4-cycle so treewidth 2, x and y mutually reachable. 435 random stopping forest games contained 0 mutually reachable controlled pairs. K_1 of thm:bounded-components indeed reads "no two distinct Max vertices are mutually reachable" and gives run length |Vmax|(2^1-1)/1.
- wa:recursion. Both halves reconstructed and correct (the only asserted steps are the choice of the constant A and T(n_0)>=1, both trivial).
- wa:warm-measured, cold column: exactly 5,9,13,18,24,31,39,48,58,69,81 for D=2..12 on both P_D and FL(D), recovered independently.

WHAT DID NOT SURVIVE. The route's central positive claim is an equivalence dressed as a reduction: PI_k implies polynomial solving at treewidth k (wa:amortised, correct), and polynomial solving at treewidth k implies PI_k in one line (solve H[X:=theta'] from scratch, take the greedy pair). So the "corrected gap" is target-equivalent to the restricted target; the route's own wa:forest-poly already settles PI_1, which next_steps offers as the open first target. Three repairable formal defects sit on top of it: the gap sentence as written is false (no beta in q(m+B)), the final non-dyadic query is outside PI_k's scope and outside the cost accounting, and FL(D)'s definition and decomposition omit u. No background job is running.
